activity.notes: ATLAS records only a representative activity point around 2700 BCE, not a fabricated reign span. The Metropolitan Museum of Art notes that Gilgamesh may have been an actual king of Uruk around 2700 BCE, while Cambridge scholarship places a historical Gilgamesh in the early third millennium BCE and distinguishes a possible historical core from later epic embellishment.

sources.title: Gilgamesh, Humbaba and the Land of the Erin-Trees — IRAQ
sources.citation_text: Hansman summarizes the Sumerological view that Gilgamesh was a historical fifth king of Uruk's first dynasty, broadly placed between 2700 and 2650 BCE, while distinguishing later unhistorical epic motifs.

sources.title: Gilgamesh — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum notes that no contemporary information survives, but that a historical Gilgamesh would have lived around 2700 BCE.
